title: Deuterium micro-heater self-anneal heals variable-retention trap cells in field
idea: H (as deuterium): package the die in a sealed D2-loaded cavity and embed polysilicon micro-heaters under each bank; when retention telemetry shows a bank's weak-cell count rising, its data is migrated out and the bank is held at ~300 C for seconds so deuterium re-passivates Si/SiO2 interface and GIDL traps (Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier breaking far better than Si-H).
why: Attacks the aging-driven growth of the trap-assisted leakage tail (fact 3); keeping tail cells healed over life could hold refresh at 2-4x longer intervals, cutting refresh energy ~50%.

title: Helium nanocavity gettering layer beneath every storage-node junction
idea: He: implant a low-dose helium layer ~200 nm below the buried-channel access transistors and anneal it into nanocavities whose inner surfaces chemisorb Fe, Cu, Ni and Au, so a gettering sink sits within diffusion range of every storage junction instead of at the wafer backside; the helium used is grams per fab-year, immune to the Qatar outage.
why: Metal deep levels drive the SRH generation behind junction-leakage tail cells (fact 3); proximity gettering could pull the tail in ~1 decade, giving 2-4x longer worst-cell retention.

title: LiPON ionic back-gate puts idle subarrays into deep-Vt hibernation
idea: Li: put a thin-film-battery-style LiPON electrolyte plus Li reservoir under each subarray, separated from the silicon by an Al2O3 Li-blocking liner; a ~1 V, ~10 ms pulse builds an ionic double layer that shifts access-transistor Vt up ~0.3-0.5 V for subarrays idle for seconds, and is reversed before reactivation.
why: Idle refresh is 16-33% of idle power (fact 3); a 0.4 V Vt lift cuts subthreshold leakage ~10^4-10^5, so cold pages need ~100x fewer refreshes on OS-idle timescales.

title: Boron arsenide spreader flattens hotspots so refresh tracks average temperature
idea: B: bond a cubic boron arsenide layer (thermal conductivity ~1,300 W/m-K) between the DRAM die and the hot logic or HBM base die, shrinking intra-die temperature gradients from ~10-15 C to ~2 C, so the refresh rate, which is set by the hottest mat, can be specified for the mean temperature.
why: Refresh interval is dictated by worst-temperature cells (fact 3); removing a 10 C hotspot roughly halves the required refresh rate in HBM stacks above accelerators, recovering bandwidth and ~10% idle power.

title: Diamond inversion-channel access transistor with week-long retention
idea: C: build the access device as an inversion-channel diamond MOSFET (phosphorus-doped n-type diamond with an Al2O3 gate, p-channel inversion) grown as diamond-on-Si; the 5.5 eV gap makes intrinsic carrier density ~10^-27 cm^-3, so off-current is set only by defects and storage nodes could hold charge for days.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) and frees capacitor margin so Cs can shrink (fact 1); retention margin ~10^5x larger, with cost hinging on heteroepitaxial diamond quality.

title: Liquid-nitrogen immersion DRAM pods eliminate refresh and cut wire energy
idea: N: run pooled CXL memory sleds immersed in 77 K liquid nitrogen made on site from air (no helium); subthreshold and junction leakage fall >10^6 so refresh can be disabled, Vt variation tightens, and copper resistance drops ~5x, enabling lower-swing I/O.
why: Kills refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) and lowers data-movement energy (fact 5); cryocooling costs ~10 W per W at 77 K, so the net win targets capacity pools where DRAM idle power dominates.

title: Post-test oxygen-vacancy trimming raises Vt of leakage-tail cells only
idea: O: use an oxide-semiconductor access FET with an oxygen-exchange TaOx gate liner; at wafer test, locate the ~0.01% leakage-tail cells and apply a per-cell high-field gate pulse that pumps oxygen into the channel near the drain, annihilating donor vacancies and permanently raising that cell's Vt ~0.2 V.
why: The tail, not the median, sets refresh (fact 3); trimming the worst 1e-4 of cells could extend the refresh interval 4-10x without touching the rest of the array.

title: Fluorinated alumina electret plane gives every access transistor built-in back bias
idea: F: bury a fluorine-implanted Al2O3 layer under the active area; Al2O3:F holds a stable negative fixed charge (~5e12 cm^-2) that acts as a permanent negative body bias, raising Vt and suppressing subthreshold leakage without a pumped VBB rail or heavy channel doping.
why: Deletes the body-bias charge pump from the periphery (fact 7) and lowers the channel doping that sharpens junction fields and GIDL (fact 3); ~2-3x lower leakage at equal on-current.

title: Polarization-doped AlGaN access channel eliminates random dopant fluctuation
idea: Al: build the access transistor in a compositionally graded AlGaN layer whose polarization gradient creates fixed 3D charge (polarization doping) instead of impurity atoms, so channel and junction 'doping' is set by a continuous Al-fraction grade identical in every cell.
why: Random dopant fluctuation in ~20 nm channels is a principal source of the Vt spread that makes the 13 fA tail (fact 3); dopant-free channels could tighten sigma-Vt ~2x and extend refresh 2-4x, if GaN-on-Si dislocation leakage is tamed.

title: Silicon-on-nothing pocket removes the storage-node junction's bottom area
idea: Si: use an empty-space-in-silicon process (etch a hole array, hydrogen-anneal so silicon migrates and seals a void) to place a vacuum pocket beneath each storage-node diffusion, leaving the junction floating with only its sidewall touching the body.
why: Junction generation leakage scales with depleted area/volume (fact 3); deleting the bottom face cuts that component ~2-5x and stops substrate minority-carrier collection that disturbs neighbor cells.

title: Lattice-matched GaP storage-node junction moves depletion into wide-gap material
idea: P (as GaP): selectively regrow a thin n+ GaP contact (2.26 eV gap, only 0.4% lattice mismatch to Si) on the silicon access transistor so the junction depletion region, where SRH generation happens, sits in GaP with ~10^7x lower intrinsic carrier density, while the channel stays silicon.
why: SRH junction leakage is proportional to n_i (fact 3); relocating even part of the depletion region into GaP could cut junction leakage by orders of magnitude while keeping silicon drive current.

title: Atomically thin junctionless sulfide access switch with no p-n junction
idea: S: make the access device a uniformly doped bilayer SnS2 or MoS2 ribbon with no source/drain junctions; the ~1.3 nm body is fully depleted by the gate in the off state, so there is no junction volume for SRH generation and no drain-overlap region for band-to-band tunnelling.
why: Removes both junction leakage and GIDL (fact 3), the two dominant tail mechanisms of recessed silicon access transistors; off-current is limited to thermionic emission over a 1.5-2 eV barrier.

title: Epitaxial CaF2 gate insulator removes the traps behind VRT
idea: Ca: grow crystalline CaF2 (12 eV gap, within 0.6% lattice match to Si(111)) as the access-transistor gate insulator by fluoride epitaxy; its ionic, dangling-bond-free interface removes the border and interface traps whose capture/emission causes variable retention time and random-telegraph leakage.
why: VRT cells force pessimistic refresh guard-bands (fact 3); a trap-free insulator could shrink the VRT population ~10x and allow ~2x longer refresh.

title: VO2 hyper-FET access transistor gives sub-60 mV per decade switching
idea: V: place a Ge-doped VO2 film (insulator-metal transition raised above ~100 C) in series with each access transistor's bitline contact; once the gate turns on, current triggers the abrupt IMT, giving an effective subthreshold slope of a few mV/decade, so Vt can sit higher at the same on-current and wordline voltage.
why: Breaks the 60 mV/dec link between leakage and wordline voltage (facts 3, 10): either ~10^3 less off-current at the same VPP or ~0.5-1 V lower wordline boost.

title: Magnetically latched FeCo nanorelay gives true open-circuit access
idea: Fe: replace the access transistor with a vertical FeCo nanocantilever relay with Ru contacts, pulled closed electrostatically by the wordline and biased by a CoPt permanent-magnet film so it latches open or closed; the off state is a vacuum gap with zero subthreshold or junction leakage.
why: Retention becomes limited only by capacitor dielectric leakage (hours), removing refresh (fact 3); contact wear (~10^15 cycles needed) is the risk, so pair it with an SRAM/cache layer that limits per-cell switching.

title: CoZrTa magnetic inductors make refresh adiabatic, recycling bitline charge
idea: Co: integrate thin-film amorphous CoZrTa inductors in the DRAM BEOL, one per bank, so restore swings during refresh are driven as resonant LC ramps instead of abrupt switching, and charge from discharging bitlines is returned to the tank for the next row.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, fact 3) is mostly bitline CV^2; resonant/adiabatic restore can recover ~50-70%, roughly halving refresh energy.

title: Gallium-oxide access transistor exploits self-trapped holes to kill GIDL
idea: Ga: use a beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) channel for the access FET; holes generated by band-to-band tunnelling at the drain edge self-trap as immobile polarons, so they cannot carry GIDL current or charge a floating body, and the n-only material has no hole conduction path.
why: GIDL and floating-body effects drive the leakage tail and amplify row hammer (facts 3, 9); a hole-immobile channel could suppress them ~10^3 while the wide gap lowers thermal leakage further.

title: Rutile-GeO2 ambipolar BEOL logic performs refresh locally per mat
idea: Ge: use rutile GeO2, an ultrawide-gap (~4.6 eV) oxide predicted to be both n- and p-dopable, to build complementary low-leakage transistors in the BEOL directly above each mat, hosting a tiny local refresh sequencer and restore driver so refresh never toggles global decoders, I/O or long data lines.
why: Takes refresh off the shared bus (fact 3: 10-20% bandwidth) and out of periphery area (fact 7); mats refresh in parallel, recovering most refresh bandwidth and ~30% of refresh energy.

title: Selenide threshold switch builds a crosspoint one-selector-one-capacitor DRAM
idea: Se: replace the three-terminal access transistor with a two-terminal Ge-As-Se ovonic threshold switch stacked on a vertical capacitor at 4F2 crosspoint pitch; selected cells see V above threshold (~1.5 V), half-selected cells see V/2, and Se-rich, N-doped compositions push sub-threshold leakage toward the fA regime.
why: 4F2 density and stackable decks without a lateral transistor (facts 2, 4); viability needs OTS off-current ~10^3 below today's, so physics risk is honestly high.

title: Antiferroelectric ZrO2 gate gives hysteresis-free negative-capacitance access device
idea: Zr: stack a thin antiferroelectric ZrO2 layer on the access-transistor gate dielectric and shift it, via work-function offset, into the negative-slope branch of its double loop, so capacitance matching gives sub-60 mV/dec swing without the memory window of ferroelectric NC-FETs.
why: Steeper slope lets a higher Vt keep on-current, cutting off-leakage ~10x or wordline voltage ~20-30% (facts 3, 10).

title: Ruthenium redox-molecule storage node holds charge for minutes
idea: Ru: graft a monolayer of Ru-polypyridyl redox molecules on the storage electrode so stored charge lives in discrete molecular oxidation states behind an electron-transfer barrier; the access transistor writes and reads by oxidizing or reducing them, and charge loss needs thermally activated back-transfer (seconds-minutes) rather than ms-scale junction drain.
why: Retention 10^3-10^4x longer cuts refresh energy and bandwidth by the same ratio (fact 3), and redox charge density can exceed a 5 fF pillar's (fact 1).

title: XeF2-carved vacuum gap isolates storage node from passing wordline
idea: Xe: deposit a sacrificial Si or Ge spacer between the storage-node contact and the adjacent passing buried wordline, then release it with XeF2 vapor (near-infinite selectivity to oxide/nitride) through a small vent, leaving a sealed k=1 vacuum gap that weakens passing-gate field and coupling at the storage junction.
why: Passing-wordline fields drive GIDL and row-hammer charge pumping (facts 3, 9); a k=1 gap versus nitride (k~7) cuts coupling ~5x, plausibly 3-10x lower passing-gate leakage and a higher hammer threshold.

title: Cesiated vacuum nano-channel access device: off state is literal vacuum
idea: Cs: form a ~20 nm sealed vacuum gap between a cesium/oxide-coated emitter (work function ~1.5 eV) on the storage node and a bitline collector, with the wordline as gate; field emission turns on exponentially at a few volts, and the off state conducts nothing through solid matter.
why: Removes semiconductor leakage paths entirely (fact 3), leaving retention set by capacitor dielectric; Cs stability, hermetic sealing and emitter variability are the risks.

title: Hydrogen-split layer transfer stacks single-crystal silicon tiers for 3D DRAM
idea: H: for each tier, bond a hydrogen-implanted donor wafer onto the finished lower tier below 400 C and cleave at the implant plane (Smart-Cut), leaving a ~30 nm single-crystal Si film in which DUV-patterned lateral access transistors are built; donors are reused ~10x, so density comes from tiers, not EUV shrink.
why: Single-crystal channels give silicon-grade low leakage in every 3D tier (facts 2, 3) with zero EUV layers (fact 4); each tier costs a bond-and-cleave instead of a litho node.

title: Convert U.S. silicon-carbide power fabs into refresh-free SiC DRAM lines
idea: C (as SiC): retool 150/200 mm 4H-SiC power-device fabs in NC, NY and TX with existing DUV steppers to build SiC MOS 1T1C cells, whose 3.26 eV gap gave early research SiC DRAM cells orders-of-magnitude longer room-temperature retention than silicon, and sell them as a big-cell, refresh-free working-memory tier behind DRAM on CXL.
why: Raises U.S. manufacturable memory supply (U.S. ~1-2% share) with tools already installed and no EUV (fact 4), and removes refresh (fact 3); lower density means it wins on capital per usable GB, not on die density.

title: Silicon-nitride retention canary cells trigger refresh only when needed
idea: N: in every row, build one canary cell with the same DUV process but a deliberately trap-rich nitride liner at its storage contact so it leaks ~3x faster than the worst data cell; a small comparator flags when the canary drops below threshold and refreshes that row only, so refresh follows real temperature, aging and process.
why: Most rows retain >10x longer than the 64 ms spec (fact 3); hardware-ground-truth refresh could cut refresh operations 4-10x with no new litho capability.

title: Self-limiting oxidation sharpens DUV pillars into sub-10 nm access channels
idea: O: pattern ~40 nm silicon pillars with DUV and thermally oxidize them; compressive stress in curved oxide retards oxidation as the core shrinks, so it self-terminates at a nearly uniform ~8-10 nm core regardless of starting CD, which becomes a gate-all-around vertical access channel after oxide strip.
why: Converts DUV CD variation into a self-limiting physical endpoint, giving thin uniform channels (low leakage, tight Vt) below EUV dimensions without EUV (facts 3, 4).

title: Mg2Si thermoelectric film under the array cools only retention-critical mats
idea: Mg: deposit thin-film Mg2Si/Mg2Sn thermoelectric couples (abundant, non-toxic, no tellurium) in the backside BEOL with i-line patterning and drive them only under mats holding data in long-refresh mode, keeping those mats ~15-20 C below die temperature.
why: Leakage roughly halves per ~10 C, so 20 C of spot cooling allows ~4x longer refresh (fact 3); it pays only where Peltier power is below the refresh power saved, such as HBM above hot logic.

title: Anodic alumina self-ordered pores template vertical gate-all-around access pillars
idea: Al: anodize a deposited aluminum film so it self-organizes into hexagonal nanopores (pitch 25-100 nm, set by anodizing voltage), guided by a coarse DUV pre-pattern, and use the pores as a mold or hard mask for vertical channel pillars wrapped by a gate.
why: Gives ~25-40 nm pitch vertical access arrays with no EUV (fact 4) at near-zero mask cost; hexagonal packing is ~15% denser than square, with domain-boundary defects handled by redundancy.

title: Epitaxial silicon stack sets access gate length by thickness, not litho
idea: Si: grow an in-situ-doped n+/p/n+ silicon stack by CVD epitaxy so the vertical channel length (80-120 nm) is fixed by the p-layer thickness to +/-1 nm, then etch DUV-immersion SAQP pillars and wrap a gate-all-around wordline, giving a 4F2 cell at DUV-reachable F of ~18-20 nm.
why: 4F2 instead of 6F2 recovers density without EUV (fact 4), and long, uniform vertical channels shrink the subthreshold leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Solid-source phosphorus drive-in grades storage junctions to cut peak field
idea: P: instead of implanting the storage-node junction, fill the self-aligned contact hole with phosphosilicate glass and drive phosphorus in by rapid thermal anneal, forming an implant-damage-free, linearly graded junction with ~30-40% lower peak field and no added mask.
why: Trap-assisted tunnelling leakage rises exponentially with peak junction field (fact 3); a damage-free, low-field junction can cut tail leakage several-fold using only mature, non-EUV steps.

title: Chlorine atomic-layer etching thins channels one monolayer at a time
idea: Cl: thin DUV-defined vertical or lateral silicon channels with cyclic Cl2 adsorption plus low-energy ion removal, ~0.5 A per self-limiting cycle, so body-thickness variation across the array falls below ~0.3 nm regardless of the litho that defined the starting shape.
why: Body-thickness variation drives Vt spread and the leakage tail of thin-body access devices (fact 3); atomic-level uniformity substitutes for EUV-level CD control (fact 4).

title: Argon cluster-ion beam trims access-gate CD map die by die
idea: Ar: measure wordline-recess and fin CDs across each DUV-patterned wafer by scatterometry, then scan an argon gas-cluster ion beam whose local dwell time removes exactly the excess material, flattening the CD map before gate formation (location-specific processing).
why: Across-wafer CD variation widens Vt and the leakage tail (fact 3); flattening it lets DUV arrays approach EUV-grade uniformity, extending refresh ~1.5-2x.

title: KOH-etched {111} sidewall channels: crystal planes replace EUV critical dimensions
idea: K: on (110) silicon, KOH etches {111} planes ~100x slower than others, so DUV-defined trenches self-terminate on atomically flat vertical {111} walls; fins between two such walls are thinned by timed lateral undercut, giving sub-20 nm access channels whose width comes from crystal geometry and etch time, not litho.
why: Atomically smooth {111} interfaces cut interface-trap density and edge-roughness Vt scatter, tightening the leakage tail (fact 3) without EUV (fact 4).

title: Nickel-seeded lateral crystallization makes single-grain transistors in every 3D tier
idea: Ni: in a stacked 3D DRAM, deposit amorphous Si for each tier and open one DUV-defined Ni seed window per row; a 500-550 C anneal sweeps a NiSi2 front laterally (metal-induced lateral crystallization), leaving long single-grain needles where lateral access transistors are placed, followed by Ni gettering.
why: Attacks the lateral-transistor blocker of 3D DRAM (fact 2) with near-single-crystal leakage at low thermal budget, without epitaxial superlattices or EUV; residual Ni is the leakage risk.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide access transistors stacked as relaxed-pitch tiers
idea: Zn: use amorphous ZnSnO, made of abundant zinc and tin, as the access-transistor channel in BEOL tiers patterned by ArF immersion at F~20-30 nm; ZTO off-current ~1e-19 A/um gives seconds-to-minutes retention, so each tier uses a small planar capacitor and density comes from 8-16 tiers instead of EUV shrink.
why: Avoids indium/gallium and EUV chokepoints (fact 4, resources) and cuts refresh ~1000x (fact 3); going beyond IGZO gain cells by deleting scarce elements from the channel.

title: Germanium-rich sacrificial layers set lateral gate length by recess depth
idea: Ge: grow an alternating Si/SiGe superlattice, cut deep slits with DUV, then laterally recess the Ge-rich layers with a self-limiting vapor-HCl atomic-layer etch to a programmed depth; the recess depth, not lithography, sets each tier's lateral access-transistor gate length, and the regrown gate wraps the Si nanosheet.
why: Makes 26+ tier lateral 3D DRAM transistors (fact 2) with nm-controlled gate length from etch chemistry rather than EUV (fact 4); uniform Lg narrows the leakage tail.

title: KrF excimer melt-anneal recrystallizes storage-node junctions defect-free
idea: Kr: after the storage-node implant, flash the surface with a tens-of-ns 248 nm KrF excimer pulse that melts only the top ~30-50 nm, so the junction regrows by liquid-phase epitaxy, annihilating end-of-range implant loops and forming a box-shaped junction without deep diffusion.
why: End-of-range defects are SRH centers behind junction-leakage tail cells (fact 3); melt regrowth could cut tail leakage ~3-10x using mature non-EUV laser tools.

title: Strontium titanate capacitor turns relaxed DUV pitch into 10x retention
idea: Sr: since a DUV-only cell is larger, spend the extra footprint on a planar or shallow-trench MIM capacitor of ALD SrTiO3 (k~100-200) instead of 60:1 pillars, storing 10-30 fF so the same fA leakage takes 3-6x longer to cross the sense margin.
why: Turns the no-EUV area penalty into charge (fact 1) and longer refresh intervals (fact 3) while avoiding extreme-aspect pillar etch; STO leakage and crystallization temperature are the risks.

title: MoS2 grown on trench sidewalls: channel geometry set by depth
idea: Mo: etch DUV-pitch trenches and grow monolayer MoS2 conformally by MOCVD on the vertical sidewalls; each sidewall becomes a vertical 2D access channel whose length equals the step height, and an ALD gate fills the trench, giving two cells per DUV feature.
why: Doubles effective cell density per DUV pitch without EUV (fact 4), while the 0.65 nm body suppresses short-channel leakage (fact 3).

title: Silver-catalyzed wet etching carves damage-free, ultra-high-aspect access trenches
idea: Ag: use metal-assisted chemical etching, in which a DUV- or block-copolymer-patterned Ag film sinks into silicon in HF/H2O2, cutting vertical trenches and pillars at >100:1 aspect ratio with no plasma, ion damage or charging, for buried-wordline recesses and vertical channels.
why: Plasma damage at the recess-gate sidewall seeds the traps behind GIDL and VRT tails (fact 3); a damage-free room-temperature wet etch could shrink the tail and cut etch-tool capital (fact 4).

title: Tin-catalyzed bottom-up nanowire access transistors grown in place
idea: Sn: place Sn catalyst dots on storage-node landing pads with a relaxed DUV pattern, shrink them to ~10-15 nm by controlled dewetting, then grow vertical Si nanowires by Sn-catalyzed vapor-liquid-solid growth below 400 C, switching in-situ doping to form source, channel and drain, followed by an ALD gate-all-around.
why: Single-crystal gate-all-around access devices at sub-litho diameter without EUV (fact 4), at a thermal budget low enough to sit above capacitors in 3D stacks (fact 2).

title: Antimony delta-doped tunnel diodes make a bistable, refresh-free storage node
idea: Sb: grow series pairs of Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes (Sb and B delta-doped layers) epitaxially on each storage node; their negative differential resistance creates two stable node voltages held by a ~pA sustain current, so the node self-restores, and every critical dimension is an epitaxial thickness.
why: Replaces periodic refresh (fact 3) with a static hold of ~4 mW/GB at 1 pA/cell; device dimensions come from epitaxy, so no EUV is needed (fact 4).

title: LaB6 multi-beam maskless writer prints only the access-gate cut layer
idea: La: deploy a massively parallel e-beam writer (LaB6 source split into ~10^5 beamlets) dedicated to the single cut/contact layer that isolates access transistors and lands storage contacts, while every other layer uses DUV pitch multiplication; no mask set and no EUV scanner are needed.
why: Removes the EUV dependency for the 1-2 layers DUV cannot pitch-split cleanly (fact 4) at a fraction of EUV capital; throughput limits it to a few layers per wafer.

title: Cerium-oxide redox buffer pins oxide-channel stoichiometry for years-stable Vt
idea: Ce: cap DUV-patterned zinc-tin-oxide access transistors with a few-nm CeOx layer whose reversible Ce3+/Ce4+ couple absorbs or releases oxygen and hydrogen, buffering the channel's oxygen chemical potential so bias-stress and hydrogen-driven Vt drift, which raises off-current over life, is suppressed with no added lithography.
why: Oxide access devices deliver ultra-low leakage only if Vt stays put; stable Vt preserves seconds-scale retention (fact 3) over product life and makes relaxed-pitch BEOL DRAM viable without EUV.

title: Dual-mode Hf-Zr-O capacitor parks idle data as polarization, stopping refresh
idea: Hf: make the storage dielectric an HfZrO stack that behaves as a linear dielectric at DRAM bias but switches ferroelectrically under a higher 'park' voltage; when a page goes idle, the controller writes its data as remanent polarization (no refresh), and on wake restores it to charge mode, using the larger capacitor area a DUV-only cell affords for ample switched charge.
why: Idle-page refresh (16-33% of idle power, fact 3) falls to ~zero while active data keeps DRAM endurance, since fatigue accrues only per park cycle (~10^5/day), not per access.
